description: Na₆Ge₂Se₇ crystallizes in the monoclinic C2/c space group. There are four inequivalent Na¹⁺ sites. In the first Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to six Se²⁻ atoms to form NaSe₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaSe₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent GeSe₄ tetrahedra, edges with four equivalent NaSe₆ octahedra, and edges with two equivalent GeSe₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 5°. There are a spread of Na-Se bond distances ranging from 2.88-3.18 Å. In the second Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to six Se²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaSe₆ octahedra that share corners with two NaSe₆ octahedra,  a cornercorner with one GeSe₄ tetrahedra, edges with four NaSe₆ octahedra, and edges with three equivalent GeSe₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 5-39°. There are a spread of Na-Se bond distances ranging from 2.99-3.47 Å. In the third Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four Se²⁻ atoms. There are two shorter (2.83 Å) and two longer (2.90 Å) Na-Se bond lengths. In the fourth Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six Se²⁻ atoms. There are a spread of Na-Se bond distances ranging from 2.97-3.56 Å. Ge⁴⁺ is bonded to four Se²⁻ atoms to form GeSe₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two NaSe₆ octahedra,  a cornercorner with one GeSe₄ tetrahedra, and edges with four NaSe₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 20-59°. There are a spread of Ge-Se bond distances ranging from 2.33-2.41 Å. There are four inequivalent Se²⁻ sites. In the first Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to five Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom. In the second Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded to five Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing SeNa₅Ge octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-5°. In the third Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded to five Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing SeNa₅Ge octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-75°. In the fourth Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to four Na¹⁺ and two equivalent Ge⁴⁺ atoms.
